headline: Far-right defendants confront violent past at Paris trial over murder of Argentine rugby star
description: Loïk Le Priol and Romain Bouvier went on trial in the Paris criminal court on Monday for shooting and killing former rugby player Federico Martin Aramburu in March 2022. Both were members of Groupe Union Défense (GUD), a far-right student group, before it was disbanded in 2024.

headline: In Toulouse, the French government auctions off a historic monument it has held for 70 years
description: The Georges Pauilhac mansion, a stunning Art Nouveau building, is set to be sold in November. Starting price: €2.1 million.

headline: Iceland's no vote does not undermine the EU's appeal
description: Driven in part by concerns over reopening the issue of fishing rights, the Icelandic referendum at the end of August disappointed supporters of European integration. Yet the EU continues to be seen as a stable regional center of governance that many other partners still want to draw closer to.

headline: Unprecedented drop in French students' performance echoes worldwide decline
description: Reading and maths scores for 15-year-olds in France have fallen to their lowest levels since 2000, mirroring trends seen in comparable countries. Among the reasons cited to explain this global phenomenon are attitudes toward learning, the role of digital technology, the lasting effects of the Covid-19 crisis and a lack of parental involvement. In France, significant social and gender inequalities persist.
byline: Eléa Pommiers,  Sylvie Lecherbonnier and  Violaine Morin

headline: Why loneliness is now seen as a harmful epidemic for mental and physical health
description: In France, nearly one in four people reported feeling lonely in 2025. This isolation particularly affects young people and the elderly, and could be a significant source of suffering. Among the possible ways to counter it are taking part in local activities and encouraging more volunteering.
